rules.model: R-full only (validation/division/cleft_egg_reference.py and new numpy/scipy modules beside it). No engine run and nothing in src/.
rules.base: Every arm changes only what it states; all other inputs keep their registered defaults.
rules.recalibration: A/L (or the access scale kappa) on pulse Rm2 = 488 kOhm at J1 for every point. P_old on pulse Rm1 = 852 kOhm for every point (it returns the record's value unless the old membrane or the cytosol changes). Same pulse protocol and readout as registered.
rules.parameter_count: Rm2 fixes exactly one unknown. An arm adding an unknown with no measurement of its own is a curve of Em and Rm at J1 against that unknown, at fixed Rm2, over a declared range. An arm whose new quantities are measured or geometric gets single values, with ranges from those quantities' own uncertainties.
rules.base_case_check: Each arm's null setting (f = 0, G_z = 0, N = 1, P_Cl = 0, alpha = 0, beta = 1) must reproduce the prediction of record within the record's reference term; this is a unit test before any arm runs.

rules.j2: J2 is off limits: no DFS74 or J2 quantity is computed for any model, including the current one, until a revised model is frozen.
rules.combinations: Arms are run one at a time. No combination is run until the single arms are reported and the lead asks for one.

dLB74_description.text: Em remains nearly constant during the first 6-8 min of cleavage; in the next 10 min it becomes about 10 mV more negative; during the second half of cleavage it often shows a small decrease (1-3 mV) preceding the onset of second cleavage. Rm is constant initially, drops drastically from 7 till 17 min, and often shows a small increase before second cleavage. The small drop in Em coincides with the moment at which the blastomeres become apposed more closely.

arms.change: The lumen as an annular slit in the cleavage plane, divided into N radial segments from its mouth to its dead end at the bridge. Each segment has its new-membrane area (both faces) and volume w x one face. Neighbouring segments exchange by free-solution two-point electrodiffusion (the registered log-mean law, free-solution D, cross-section w x 2 pi r). The mouth segment reaches the bath through one rim access.

geometry.growth: Fixed rings: the slit [r_bridge, r_mouth] is divided into N rings of equal radial width at J1's geometry. The slit's inner edge r_in(t) moves inward as new membrane is inserted on the registered schedule, with A_face(t) = pi (r_mouth^2 - r_in(t)^2) and A_face = A_new/2. A ring switches on when r_in(t) enters it; the ring containing r_in(t) grows (its membrane area and volume), the others are fixed.
geometry.basis: bridge 0.26 mm2 (BdL73 p95, V; 0.18 kind not stated); new membrane 1.39 mm2 on both sheets (BdL73 Table II p96 and the double sheet, p92, V); egg radius 0.65 mm (dL74 p5, V); the annulus shape and the inward growth are declared (S). The mouth then lies 99 um below the egg surface, beside BdL73's groove of about 100 um at 4 min and 150 um at 8 min (p96, V), with almost parallel deep walls (p96, V)
geometry.fill: New volume appears in place in the growing ring and is filled with bath fluid at bath composition, as the registered single lumen is (reservoir supply). With N = 1 this reduces exactly to the registered rule. Stated limit: no flow along the slit; fluid drawn inward from the mouth would carry lumen fluid, so in-place bath fill understates deep-end K+ accumulation.

arms.why: K83 (p1759, V) implicates Ca2+ influx (2 mM Mn2+ cut the furrow current to 42%, 1 mM Co2+ to 52%). But no source read fixes the old membrane's Ca2+ permeability, the cytosol's Ca2+ buffering or extrusion, or Steinberg's Ca2+ activity on the activity basis. Without buffering and extrusion, an unbuffered 1-nA influx would raise free Ca2+ by about 7 uM/s in 0.78 uL (S), so R-full cannot carry Ca2+ honestly. Its electrical effect would be an inward current with a positive EMF, i.e. depolarising.

held_check_C1_for_frozen_candidates.status: HELD for frozen candidates. Not computed in this pass for any model, tests included. Its use is decided under a rule registered before its first run, when candidate models are frozen. Its Steinberg leg corresponds to J1, which is already computed, so only the B and C legs would be blind, and the judged quantity would be the shift within dL74's own series.
held_check_C1_for_frozen_candidates.why_held: It is the only blind test a revised model can face soon (J2 needs the partition, which R-full lacks); once numbers sit beside dL74's, they select.
